standard.title: Language carries cultural meaning
standard.description: recognise that language carries cultural meaning in everyday social interactions
standard.prior_knowledge: Students have used formulaic social expressions in classroom and play contexts (AC9LCH2C01, AC9LCH2C02). They have noticed that gestures and body language contribute to meaning. They have not yet examined why specific language forms are used — the cultural conventions behind politeness, address, etiquette — or identified expressions that carry cultural meaning with no direct English equivalent.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students recognise that language choices in everyday social interactions carry cultural meaning — including conventions of politeness, address, etiquette, and culturally-specific expressions — and can identify examples and explain their significance.

nodes.label: Politeness, address and social etiquette conventions
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify and use language conventions for politeness, appropriate address and social etiquette in familiar everyday contexts.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least two conventions of politeness or address in the target language and use them correctly in context — for example, distinguishing a polite request from a demand, or using appropriate address for an adult.
nodes.typical_width: Demonstrate levels of politeness in different contexts — requests, thanks, address of adults and peers; identify cultural gestures and etiquette conventions; distinguish between polite and impolite forms of the same communicative act; use appropriate language when addressing people of different ages or authority.
wider: Compare politeness conventions in the target language with English — identify where the conventions differ and what this reveals about cultural values around respect and relationship
Explore a range of everyday social contexts (greeting an elder, receiving a gift, entering someone's home) and identify the specific language and gesture conventions for each
nodes.hinge_reason: Politeness and address conventions are the foundation for all culturally appropriate social interaction. Students who do not understand why specific language forms are used cannot interpret or produce culturally appropriate communication — a prerequisite for the cultural translation and mediation work that develops across Y3-4 and beyond.

response_modes.reason: Politeness conventions require students to move from observing language use to understanding the cultural logic behind it. Explicit discussion of why a particular form is used — not just what is said — builds the cultural reasoning capacity that distinguishes background learners' insight from surface imitation.

success_criteria: Identifies at least two politeness or address conventions in the target language and can explain why each is used
Demonstrates the correct form in at least one context — for example, a polite request or appropriate address for an adult

nodes.label: Culturally-specific expressions and untranslatable language
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify expressions in the target language that carry cultural meaning — including phrases with no direct English equivalent or phrases used on specific cultural occasions.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least one expression in the target language that carries specific cultural meaning and cannot be directly translated, and explain what it means in context.
nodes.typical_width: Explore colloquial phrases, occasion-specific expressions and culturally-embedded language; discuss the cultural meaning and context of these expressions; compare with how equivalent sentiments are expressed in English; create bilingual resources that explain the cultural context of key expressions.
wider: Research a culturally-specific occasion or celebration and identify the language specifically associated with it — explain why particular expressions are used on that occasion and not others
Compare culturally-specific expressions across two or more languages known in the class — identify where untranslatability reflects different cultural values

response_modes.reason: Culturally-specific expressions are encountered rather than deduced. Students need exposure to a range of occasions, contexts and expression types before the general insight — that language encodes cultural meaning — becomes visible. Varied cultural encounters build the repertoire from which this understanding emerges.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Background learners carry authentic knowledge of culturally-specific expressions from home and community. Width investment here invites students to share and examine this knowledge — positioning them as cultural informants rather than only learners, which is both pedagogically and interpersonally valuable.
success_criteria: Identifies at least one culturally-specific expression and explains its meaning in context
Can explain why the expression does not translate directly into English

nodes.label: Non-verbal and visual cues as cultural meaning
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify how non-verbal cues — gesture, facial expression, body language — carry culturally-specific meaning in the target language, and interpret these in interaction and media texts.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least two non-verbal cues in the target language (gesture, facial expression, body language) and explain what they mean in their cultural context.
nodes.typical_width: Interpret cultural gestures and non-verbal communication conventions; identify how facial expressions and visual cues in animations, songs and stories contribute to meaning; compare non-verbal conventions between the target language community and English-speaking contexts.
wider: Analyse a short animated or video text and identify all the non-verbal cues that carry meaning — compare with a peer's reading to discuss what is shared and what is culturally interpreted

Discuss how non-verbal communication in the target language compares with gesture and body language in First Nations Australian communication — identify similarities and differences in how gesture carries meaning

response_modes.reason: Non-verbal meaning interpretation integrates politeness conventions (node 1) and cultural expression awareness (node 2) into a holistic reading of communicative acts. The teaching investment is in creating analysis tasks that require students to notice the full communicative package — verbal, non-verbal and contextual — not only words.

success_criteria: Identifies at least two non-verbal cues in the target language and explains their cultural meaning
Demonstrates or describes the correct use of at least one culturally-specific gesture or non-verbal convention
